title: But What About That One Student? Use 2×10
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Following a post on how teacher-student relationships inevitably break down and need repair, Dave Stuart Jr. addresses teachers' next question: what about the student you cannot begin a relationship with at all? His answer is the 2x10 strategy from Raymond Wlodkowski's observational research, relayed through Angela Watson: for ten consecutive class periods, talk for two minutes with the hardest-to-reach student about a non-school topic of their choosing. He cites Wlodkowski's reported 85 percent improvement in that student's behavior and gains in the whole class, and reports consistent results from using it with four of his own 120 students. He frames the tactic as bounded and sustainable, a way to act on the hardest cases without draining time owed to every student, while building credibility with the target student and bystanders. The piece is short but practical relationship-and-behavior craft, tied to his Care, Competence, Passion and Repair view of teacher credibility.
points: 2x10 is a time-boxed relationship intervention: two minutes a day for ten days on a non-school topic the student chooses.
Wlodkowski's observations, as cited, show large behavior gains for the target student and spillover improvement across the rest of the class, likely via increased teacher credibility.
The method does not have to go smoothly; early conversations may be awkward, and the point is persistent professional effort rather than perfection.
Its bounded size helps teachers do something for the hardest students without an unsustainable time cost or guilt.
Repair is added to Care, Competence and Passion as part of teacher credibility, since relationships will break down.
quotes: If you cannot identify and repair faltering student-teacher relationships, you’re bound to be befuddled by the change in student motivation you’ll witness when you unintentionally offend a student.
The 2×10 strategy is simple: for 10 class periods in a row, you speak to your hardest-to-reach student(s) for two minutes straight on a non-school topic of their choosing.
According to Wlodkowski, when teachers used 2×10 with their toughest students, he observed “an 85-percent improvement in that one student’s behavior.” And the improvement didn’t stop there.
Sometimes these two-minute conversations have been awkward — especially on the first day or two when it’s hard to elicit more than monosyllabic responses.

But here’s the consistent result: in all cases where I’ve completed a full 2×10 intervention, that student’s behavior and motivation have improved. Where once relationships did not exist, now relationships do.
Avoid pouring an unsustainable time chunk into reaching our hardest to reach students — after all, there are ~30 on each of my rosters and I owe my work to all of them.
